title: fullcycle's PATH scan forks readlink once per symlink, so its cost is the operator's PATH and not the project
body:
`_fullcycle_path_links` (`lib/cmd/fullcycle:129`) walks every entry in `$PATH` and forks `readlink` **once per symlink** to decide whether the link points into `PROJECT_ROOT`. The cost is therefore a function of the operator's `$PATH`, not of the project, and nothing in the output says so.

## Measured, 2026-09-06, on the development machine

    symlinks in PATH:         1,429   (/opt/homebrew/bin alone holds 1,301, nearly all symlinks)
    readlink forks per call:  1,533
    wall cost per call:        2.68s
    tests/unit/fullcycle.bats: 142.20s for 33 tests  (user 43.56s, sys 71.68s)

**Sys time at nearly double user time is the signature**: this is process churn, not computation. Every `fullcycle` invocation pays ~2.7s before doing any work, and the suite invokes it dozens of times.

## Why it went unnoticed

**The cost lives in the operator's environment.** A CI runner with a lean `PATH` carries a handful of symlinks and the scan is instant; a Homebrew development machine is close to the worst case available. So the function is fast for everyone who measured it and slow for the person actually running the suite, and the difference is invisible in the code.

It presents as a hang. It was reported as "quiet for 1m30s" against a test that had already passed, because the elapsed time attaches to whichever test is running rather than to the scan inside it.

## The fix

`find` narrows the candidates in one fork per directory instead of one per symlink:

    find "$p" -maxdepth 1 -type l -lname "$PROJECT_ROOT"/'*'

    per-symlink readlink:  2.68s
    one find per dir:      0.04s      (22 forks rather than 1,533)

**`find` must be an ACCELERATOR and never the decision.** `-lname` glob-matches the whole pattern, so a `PROJECT_ROOT` containing `[`, `*` or `?` would match differently from the existing `case "$(readlink "$f")" in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/*)`, whose left half is literal. So the candidates `find` returns are re-tested with the original `case`, unchanged. Over-matching is then harmless and under-matching is prevented by escaping the metacharacters in the pattern. Behaviour cannot move; only the number of forks does.

`-lname` is verified present on BSD `find` with a positive control -- a link into the fake project root matched, a link to `/bin/ls` did not. rc=0 alone would not have separated "matched nothing" from "flag unsupported", which is the failure this project refuses everywhere else.
